title: Bridgewell Homeowner Service Contracts — Premium Collection, Nonpayment Suspension and Reinstatement
content:
## 1. Applying payments

A premium payment on one of Bridgewell's Homeowner Service Contracts is applied to the premium balance, oldest unpaid charge first. The installment that drives nonpayment handling is the oldest unpaid one: the billing period start of the oldest monthly installment or annual premium charge not fully covered by payments and credits applied oldest charge first.

## 2. Suspension for nonpayment

Service is suspended only when an installment remains unpaid more than the payment grace period (in calendar days) after the installment's due date; the count starts the day after the due date, and suspension applies from the first day after the grace period ends.

While a contract is suspended for nonpayment, no service request is accepted and no contractor is dispatched.

## 3. Reinstatement

A suspended contract is reinstated only when the premium balance is zero or less after payment and the payment posts no later than the suspension cure period (in calendar days) after the contract was suspended; the count starts the day after the suspended date and the boundary day itself qualifies. Reinstatement does not restart the waiting period and does not change term dates, and failures first reported while suspended are not covered.

## 4. Cancellation for nonpayment

A suspended contract whose balance is not cleared is cancelled for nonpayment once more than the suspension cure period's calendar days have passed after the contract was suspended, counted from the day after the suspended date. On a nonpayment cancellation the cancellation admin fee is not charged and no refund is due, and premium already billed for periods before the cancellation remains owed. Payments received on a cancelled or expired contract are applied to its remaining balance but never reinstate it.

All three clocks run from dates on the system record: the installment's due date (its billing period start) and the contract's suspended date.

## Timeline illustration (hypothetical dates, 30-day grace and 30-day cure periods)

| Date | Day count | Position under the clauses |
|---|---|---|
| March 1 | due date of the oldest unpaid installment | count has not started |
| March 31 | day 30 after the due date | still within the grace period; no suspension |
| April 1 | first day after the grace period | suspension applies from this day |
| May 1 | day 30 after the April 1 suspension | a payment posting today that leaves the balance at zero or less reinstates |
| May 2 | day 31 | more than 30 days have passed; the contract is cancelled for nonpayment if the balance is not cleared |

## Questions this clause answers

**A payment posts on the last day of the cure period but leaves 10.00 owing — is the contract reinstated?** No. Reinstatement needs both conditions: the balance zero or less after the payment, and the payment posted no later than the boundary day.

**Does reinstatement give the customer a new waiting period or new term dates?** No to both; the term dates stay as they were.

**Is a failure first reported during the suspension covered once the contract is reinstated?** No.
